ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-02-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Rodriguez, MD
Department: Pediatric Orthopedics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Persistent limp and decreased activity over the past 6 weeks

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 7-year-old male returning for follow-up evaluation approximately one month after his initial presentation for progressive limping and right hip pain. His parents note that he used to be very active but now avoids running and complains of stiffness in the morning. There is no fever, rash, trauma, or recent illness. The child denies night sweats or weight loss.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

He is of normal weight and height and has met all developmental milestones.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal second cousin: Legg-Calve-Perthes disease
- Father: seasonal allergies
- Mother: healthy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student - 2nd grade.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical exam, internal rotation and abduction of the right hip elicit discomfort. Gait assessment reveals mild antalgic walking and subtle pelvic drop on the left when standing on the right leg. There is no joint effusion, warmth, or swelling noted.

IMAGING:
A pelvic radiograph is obtained and shown below.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive limping and intermittent right hip pain for the past 3 weeks

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
His mother reports that he has been otherwise well, with no recent fever, trauma, or illness. The pain initially occurred only after prolonged running or playing but has now become more persistent. He has no complaints of pain in his knee or foot. The patient denies night sweats, weight loss, or malaise. He has no history of travel, tick bites, or recent infections.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
His past medical history is unremarkable, and his immunizations are up to date.

MEDICATIONS:
He is not taking any medications.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
There is no family history of rheumatologic or orthopedic conditions.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
His academic and social development are age appropriate.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, he is afebrile and appears well. He walks with an antalgic gait, favoring the right side. There is no visible swelling, redness, or warmth of the hip. Passive internal rotation and abduction of the right hip are limited and mildly painful. The left hip and both knees are normal on examination. Neurovascular status is intact bilaterally.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies reveal normal ESR, CRP, and white blood cell count.

IMAGING:
Plain radiographs of the pelvis show increased density and slight flattening of the right femoral head, while the left femoral head appears normal. There is no joint space widening or signs of effusion.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. Emily Watson, MD
Department: Pediatric Orthopedics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Intermittent right hip pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 7-year-old male returning for follow-up evaluation, having been previously seen in January and February 2020 for progressive limping and persistent right hip pain. He is brought to the pediatrician by his mother due to a 3-month history of intermittent right hip pain. The pain is described as dull and worsens with activity, sometimes radiating to the knee. The mother reports that her son has been limping, especially after playing soccer.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal second cousin: Legg-Calve-Perthes disease
- Father: seasonal allergies
- Mother: healthy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student - 2nd grade.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the boy walks with a slight limp favoring his right leg. Range of motion of the right hip is limited, particularly with internal rotation and abduction. There is no erythema, warmth, or swelling of the hip or knee.

IMAGING:
An anteroposterior radiograph of the pelvis is obtained and reveals slight flattening and increased density of the right femoral head.
